show_hn.story_text: Here in the north of England clear nights are at a premium, and it's never guaranteed that you'll be able to see anything but cloud. It sits in the Mac's menu bar and refreshes the forecast every 30 minutes. Show HN: Jev-pages – Building landing pages real time with Jev
show_hn.story_text:
An experiment using Jev to generate landing pages in real time. Jev is great at picking between different options so I attempted to break down the langing page UI into a set of choices for the model to choose from. How this works:
1. Users type what kind of page they want and Jev decides what each line is (headline, fact, assertion etc.)
2. Jev makes choices for each layer of the page (opening, stage, light, depth etc.). Parameterizing design is hard (impossible?) but this took some tuning with Claude 
3. A full page is constructed with a single call of about 90 questions. Of course using an LLM would be more prudent for step 1, but I wanted to check the limits of Jev's understanding (it works pretty well in my opinion!).

show_hn.story_text:
When reading a history book, I sometimes have a hard time internalizing when the events are taking place. Sure, I know the dates, but it takes a bit of effort to put them in a broader context, to understand where in history they belong. What usually helps is to put them in relation to other contemporaneous events.
To play around with this, I've made Meanwhile Map. You select a date and a time window, then scroll around the world map to see a list of contemporaneous events.

In general MTB trails on OSM could be greatly improved, especially when it comes to IMBA ratings and I wanted to lower the barrier to entry to contributing to OSM. Key features: * Load satellite, lidar or OSM GPS traces to verify trail paths
* Dedicated keybindings for quickly tagging a trail's IMBA rating and other actions
* Add, edit and split trails to improve trail accuracy
* Circle a group of trails to add or update a trail network
* Load all trails in a given state or region (US and Canada supported to start)
* Upload to OSM as a changeset Hope some folks find this useful, let me know what feedback you have!
